source.title: ConceptPrune: Concept Editing in Diffusion Models via Skilled Neuron Pruning
source.authors: Ruchika Chavhan; Da Li; Timothy Hospedales

record.file_problem: none; the full paper and appendix are present.
record.tranche_reason: Tests whether adversarial prompts can elicit concepts after editing, and whether a pruning method resists such attacks, in text-to-image diffusion models rather than LLMs.
record.gate_note: The reported adversarial attack outcomes are rows. The paper also reports ordinary concept-erasure and retained-capability results, but those do not establish near-chance targeted accuracy; the attack tables most directly bear on the versions tested here. Cited attack findings from prior work are not recorded as results.
record.test_reason: The study reports its own adversarial-prompt attacks (Ring-A-Bell, MMA-Diffusion, UnlearnDiffAtk) on concept-erased Stable Diffusion models. It measures whether erased concepts (nudity, Van Gogh style, objects) come back, for baselines and for its pruning method. This is a new setting (text-to-image diffusion, not LLM knowledge) with results on prompt-based recovery (E) and on a claimed robust method (F).
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that ConceptPrune erases concepts training-free and permanently, with strong robustness to attacks that break prior erasure methods. They do not frame the 64.8% nudity ASR as a limitation; they present it as significantly lower than SDv2 and SLD.
record.recipe_differences: Training-free, Wanda-inspired skilled-neuron identification and weight pruning in diffusion-model FFNs; tested against concept-editing baselines and adversarial prompts, not the cited LLM unlearning recipes.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcomes vary by attack type and target concept: Ring-A-Bell, MMA-Diffusion, and UnlearnDiffAtk give different results; UnlearnDiffAtk results also vary across art style, nudity, and object targets.
record.problems: Attack tables report no uncertainty estimates. The evidence concerns text-to-image diffusion models, not LLMs; the reported attack sets cover only some prompting attacks in the claim. ConceptPrune's UnlearnDiffAtk nudity ASR is 64.8%.
record.rows_left_out: Ordinary concept-erasure and retained-capability results (Tables 1, 3, and 5; Section 5) are not included as rows because they do not directly measure attack-induced recovery. No attack-table results were left out.

untested.parts: LLMs and near-chance targeted-knowledge accuracy. Retained capability is not measured under attack.
No fine-tuning or relearning attack on any model.
No activation-direction ablation and no analysis of blocking versus deleting.
Only optimized adversarial prompts in diffusion models. No plain rephrasing, other languages, or in-context information.
ConceptPrune is not tested against fine-tuning, quantization, or internal-edit attacks. It is tested only against three prompt attacks.

missing.what: No-attack erasure levels needed to read recovery: nudity reduction ESD 88%, UCE 85.6%, ConceptPrune 94.1% (47 of 796 prompts); erased-class accuracies (e.g., UCE Tench 0.0, ConceptPrune Church 1.9); style erasure metrics
Retained capability (FID / CLIP on COCO30k, preserved-class accuracy) for ConceptPrune and baselines, bearing on A's 'keeps general ability'

record.verdict_notes: The setting is text-to-image diffusion (SD v1.5), not LLMs, so all links are T3 and the system differs from the versions' originals. SDv2 rows are relinked to none because SDv2 is filtered-data training, not unlearning. SLD is inference-time guidance and is kept with caution. Row states describe recovery of the erased concept (E's effect); for F, absent recovery means support. UnlearnDiffAtk ASRs have no stated no-attack baseline in the table, and there are no uncertainty estimates. No fine-tuning attack was run on the pruned model, which leaves F's robustness to relearning open.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test LLM unlearning, near-chance targeted-knowledge accuracy, or the full set of attacks in the claim.
No fine-tuning or relearning attack is tested.
No activation-direction ablation or analysis of access blocking versus deletion is tested.
Tests specified adversarial prompt attacks in diffusion models, not ordinary rephrasing, other languages, or in-context information.
Tests ConceptPrune against the reported adversarial attacks, not against fine-tuning, activation edits, quantization, or all prompting attacks in the claim.

relation.reason: It reports whether erased concepts return under attack.

tranche.reason: The paper tests its own method and the baselines under adversarial prompts in text-to-image diffusion: a new setting with a result on the claim.

source_check.notes: Table 2 is flattened. Columns: ESD, UCE, SLD, FMN, SD2.0, Ours. Rows: Ring-A-Bell and MMA (% reduction vs SD), then UnlearnDiffAtk (ASR). The study uses SD-v1.5, and CA has no nudity or object results. No-attack reductions (94.1, 88, 85.6) are on I2P, not the attack prompt sets. Attack results have no uncertainty.

statements.correction: This study: ConceptPrune (SD-v1.5) nudity reduction vs pre-trained SD under MMA 95.6. The no-attack reduction is 94.1, on I2P prompts.
statements.problem: The statement makes no claim about this study. Its cited row T2-MMA-CP does not appear in it, so the citation dangles.

statements.correction: The study reports attack success on image concepts in Stable Diffusion: nudity (NudeNet), ImageNette objects (ResNet-50) and Van Gogh style (top-1/top-3 classifier).
ESD (SD-v1.5) nudity reduction vs SD: 88 with no attack (I2P), 87.3 under MMA, 52.8 under Ring-A-Bell. UnlearnDiffAtk nudity ASR 76.1.
statements.problem: The statement says nothing about this study, though it cites the ESD rows T2-MMA-ESD and T2-RAB-ESD.

statements.correction: Model: Stable Diffusion-v1.5 (Sec 5). UnlearnDiffAtk nudity ASR: ESD 76.1, UCE 93.2, FMN 97.9 (SLD 82.4, SDv2 73.8). CA has no nudity or object results. Ring-A-Bell nudity reduction vs SD: ESD 52.8, UCE 67.6, FMN 5.60. UnlearnDiffAtk Van Gogh top-3 ASR: ESD 76, FMN 90, CA 92, UCE 100. FMN object ASR: Parachute 100, Tench 100, Garbage Truck 98, Church 96. Attack results carry no error bars; the only ± is gender reversal, 87 ± 12%.
statements.problem: Nudity ASR 76.1-97.9 is UnlearnDiffAtk only, for ESD/UCE/FMN; CA was not run on nudity; Ring-A-Bell gives reductions, not ASR. The study uses SD-v1.5, not v1.4. Its only uncertainty is for gender reversal.
